novel.justification: This heterogeneous-baseline conditional mean-movement restriction is substantive and is not inherited from the common-zero-baseline bounded-CAS result. It is satisfied by random-coefficient location models \(Y_2^Q(d)=a(X,U)+c(X,U)d\) with \(|c(X,U)|\le K\) almost surely, and more generally by absolutely continuous dose-response schedules whose individual marginal effects are bounded by \(K\). Such caps are credible for policy doses or temperature exposures over a prespecified compact range.

Andrews and Shi (2013) develop inference based on conditional moment inequalities; they do not provide this model's necessary-and-sufficient support-local obstacle compatibility certificate or its full-law affine attainment argument.
Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2011) provide convex sharp-identification-region logic; they do not supply the present continuum obstacle clipping and certified mesh-Hausdorff map for WAOSS.
Freyberger and Horowitz (2015) obtain sharp bounds from finite linear programs under discrete-support shape restrictions; they do not provide the continuum-to-mesh clipping certificate used here.

Freyberger (2017) shows that data can estimate an upper bound on the diameter of an identified set in nonparametric instrumental-variable models; it does not establish this panel obstacle identified set or its WAOSS endpoint program.
Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018) optimize policy-relevant weighted functionals under convex restrictions on marginal treatment effects; they do not derive this conditional-completion frontier.

Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) obtain uniformly valid calibrated projection for finite moment-inequality systems; the present inference theorem separately constructs the boundary-cell and continuum-discretization ingredients for this WAOSS model.
Belloni, Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015) provide uniform series-regression theory; they do not give the signed-measure, obstacle-program, and ratio composition specialized here.
Cattaneo, Chandak, Jansson, and Ma (2024) provide boundary-adaptive conditional-density inference; they do not supply the present primitive boundary-cell conditional-mean band or WAOSS program.

Sasaki and Ura (2025) study panel estimands and inference with slow movers; that work does not establish the full-law sharp WAOSS completion set or repair the baseline-conditional support gap proved here.
